children: Tata Steel's consolidated revenue rises 11.5 per cent to Rs 65,436 crore in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA grows 17 per cent year-on-year to Rs 10,665 crore; Noel Tata to step down on November 11

Tata Steel posted a 16.2 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit for the September quarter of FY27, supported by higher revenue and improved operating performance, while Noel Naval Tata is set to retire as the company's vice-chairman on November 11.

Consolidated profit after tax (PAT) rose to Rs 3,699.59 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs 3,183.09 crore in the corresponding period last fiscal, the company said in a regulatory filing on Friday.
Revenue from operations increased 11.5 per cent to Rs 65,436.24 crore from Rs 58,689.29 crore a year earlier.

Consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) stood at Rs 10,665 crore, with a margin of around 16 per cent. EBITDA increased 17 per cent year-on-year and 14 per cent sequentially.
In India, revenue stood at Rs 42,653 crore, while EBITDA was Rs 10,634 crore, translating into an operating margin of 25 per cent.

Crude steel production in India increased 7 per cent sequentially to 6.18 million tonnes during the quarter, while deliveries rose 16 per cent to 5.98 million tonnes, reflecting improved production and sales volumes.
The company incurred capital expenditure of around Rs 3,280 crore during the quarter, taking its first-half spending to Rs 6,860 crore.

Key projects under execution include the 4.8 million tonnes per annum (MTPA) capacity expansion at Neelachal Ispat Nigam Limited, a 0.7 MTPA Hot Rolled Pickling and Galvanising Line, and a 300,000-tonne tinplate expansion.

Tata Steel's net debt stood at Rs 91,423 crore at the end of the quarter, with its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 2.4 times. Group liquidity was Rs 40,076 crore, including cash and cash equivalents of around Rs 10,300 crore.
Separately, Noel Naval Tata will retire as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director and Vice-Chairman of the board with effect from the close of business hours on November 11, 2026.

T V Narendran, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director of Tata Steel, said the company continued to advance its volume and value growth strategy in India, supported by customer engagement and a resilient supply chain despite geopolitical and economic uncertainties and elevated raw material costs.

He said the automotive and special products businesses delivered a strong performance, while downstream sales continued to grow. The company is also expanding its presence in emerging segments, including shipbuilding, data centres and containers.
Narendran added that the company was making steady progress on its capacity expansion and downstream growth projects.
